Three Earths

The panels are Porcelain on every board: its fonts, colours, buttons, list and tiles, in your Dense layout. What changes is the Earth under them and the space around it, which is where God's eye lives. Same theatre view, same data on all six: the server's stored feeds, newest 28 Nov 2026 03:08 UTC.

A

Real Earth, smoked panels

God's eye's NASA photo and black space, with Porcelain's parts made slightly see-through so the Earth shows under them. There is no blur, which was what made Safari slow before.

What it keepsThe real colours of the land: deserts, forests, snow. It is the most "God's eye" of the three.
What it costsColour markers compete with the photo's browns and greens, which is why orange had to go. Picture tiles are also the heaviest ground to draw.
In the appThe Photo ground already exists. Only the panels change.
B

Ink Earth

My pick

The icon at full size: black seas, charcoal land with hairline borders and a little relief, and a pale atmosphere along the sunlit edge. In light mode the globe hangs in white porcelain space; in dark mode it sits in night.

Why I pick itIt is the brand and the map in one picture. Every colour marker reads on black, and nothing in the ground pretends to know more than a border.
What it costsNothing extra: it is a vector style with no picture tiles, so it is lighter to draw than the photo. The photo stays one click away under Settings › Ground.
To check in the appWhether MapLibre's globe leaves the space around it transparent, so the white or night page shows through. I have not tried that yet.
C

Silver Earth

NASA's photo with the colour taken out: real mountains, rivers and coasts in greys. In light mode it is a pale porcelain Earth on white; in dark mode a dim silver one on night.

What it keepsThe terrain detail of the photo, without its colours fighting the markers.
What it costsThe light version is soft: land and sea are both pale, so at a glance it reads less clearly than A or B. It still loads picture tiles, like the photo.
In the appIt is the Mono ground recoloured: warm grey on white instead of cold blue on black.
Next

Once you pick

  1. Which Earth is the default: A, B or C. The other grounds stay in Settings either way.
  2. Panels solid (B, C) or see-through (A), whichever Earth you pick.
  3. Then I draw every panel and screen in it before building anything: each kind of card (event, aircraft, ship, satellite, base, outage), the layers sheet and key, search, Settings, feeds, person and country dossiers, follow mode, look down, Connections and Investigate pages, empty and dead-feed states.
